english_paragraphs: One night in early 2016, after keepers at New Zealand's National Aquarium in Napier had left, an octopus named Inky crept through an aperture in the mesh atop its tank. The fugitive presumably dropped to the floor, crossed the room, and compressed its elastic body into a drain, whose pipe stretched some 50 metres to the Pacific.

Staff reconstructed that route from the slime residue it deposited. Inky had resided in captivity since 2014, when a fisherman retrieved it from a crayfish pot off Napier. The breakout went unreported for about three months. Made public in April 2016, the story travelled the globe.

Such agility stems from an octopus's pliable body, which has no skeleton or shell. Its only hard part is its beak, so any crevice that accommodates the beak will do. Roughly two-thirds of its 500 million neurons lie in the limbs, which handle sensory input and react with some autonomy.

Its wits are as versatile as its anatomy. A giant Pacific octopus in Seattle learned to open screw-top jars, needing 15 minutes at the outset, later about two. In a 2010 study, octopuses came to discriminate between two strangers, a feeder and one who touched them with a bristly stick, adopting a different hue and posture for each.

In July 2012 the Cambridge Declaration on Consciousness listed octopuses among animals possessing the neurological substrates for conscious awareness. A November 2021 UK government review recommended treating them as sentient, and the Animal Welfare (Sentience) Act encompassed them in April 2022. None of this proves an inner life. Inky, somewhere beyond the pipe, remained wholly oblivious to the debate.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 2016年初的一个夜晚，在新西兰内皮尔国家水族馆的**饲养员**(keepers)离开之后，一只名叫Inky的章鱼从水箱**顶部**(atop)**网罩**(mesh)上的一道**开口**(aperture)**悄悄爬了出去**(crept)。这名**逃犯**(fugitive)**想必**(presumably)落到了地上，穿过了房间，然后把它**有弹性的**(elastic)身体**挤**(compressed){{（压缩/挤压）|compressed}}进了一个排水口，排水口的管道**延伸**(stretched)约50米，通到太平洋。

工作人员根据它**留下**(deposited)的**黏液**(slime)**残迹**(residue)，**还原了**(reconstructed){{（使重现）|reconstructed}}这条路线。Inky从2014年起就一直**居住**(resided)在**圈养**(captivity)环境中；那一年，一名渔民从内皮尔附近海域的一个**捕龙虾的笼子**(crayfish pot)里**取出了**(retrieved)它。
{{（专门捕虾的笼子）|crayfish pot}}这次**越狱**(breakout)大约三个月都**没有被报道**(unreported)。2016年4月被公开之后，这个故事传遍了**全球**(globe)。

这样**灵巧的身手**(agility){{（动作敏捷）|agility}}**源于**(stems from)章鱼**柔韧的**(pliable)身体，这种身体没有**骨骼**(skeleton)，也没有外壳。它唯一坚硬的部位是**喙**(beak)，所以任何**容得下**(accommodates)喙的**缝隙**(crevice)都行。它的5亿个**神经元**(neurons)中，大约三分之二位于**腕足**(limbs)里；腕足处理**感官输入**(sensory input)，并且在作出反应时有一定的**自主性**(autonomy)。

它的**机智/智慧**(wits)和它的**身体构造**(anatomy)一样**用途广泛**(versatile)。西雅图的一只巨型太平洋章鱼学会了打开螺旋盖的**罐子**(jars)，**起初/最开始的时候**(at the outset)需要15分钟，后来大约要两分钟。在2010年的一项研究中，章鱼逐渐能够**区分**(discriminate)两个陌生人，一个是**喂食者**(feeder)，另一个用带刺毛的棍子碰它们；章鱼对每个人**采用**(adopting)不同的**颜色**(hue)和**姿态**(posture)。

2012年7月，《剑桥意识宣言》把章鱼列入了**具备**(possessing)**神经**(neurological)**基质**(substrates)的动物之列，这种神经基质专门用来**有意识的**(conscious)**认识**(awareness)。2021年11月，英国政府的一份评估报告建议认定它们**有感知力**(sentient)；而《动物福利（感知）法》于2022年4月把它们**纳入了/包括**(encompassed)其中。这些都不能证明（章鱼）有**内心**(inner)世界。Inky在管道另一头的某个地方，始终对这场争论**全然**(wholly)**不知**(oblivious)。
